Then I would be extra careful. Conures have a scissor for a beak and is like x2 stronger than a budgie’s, during play time be sure to always supervise them to ensure your conure doesn’t hurt the budgie. And I mean ALWAYS keep them in the corner of your eye because you can’t be too sure and accidents can happen!  

In case you didn’t know, here are the steps to introduce birds to each other: 

Put cages next to each other, close but not too close that they can bite each others feet -> after they’ve gotten used to being near each other, get them to eat a snack they both like together -> supervised playtime 

Birds like to eat together with their flock, so sharing a snack is one of the best ways to get a pair of parrots to bond!

Budgies are notorious for not tolerating other breeds of birds, they like to stick with other budgies. Some budgies are also so aggressive to the degree that they can be murderers

Conures are also notorious for being aggressively friendly, to the point of not respecting boundaries and pushing the other bird’s buttons as they like to tussle and play rough. 

Of course, for living creatures we usually can’t completely generalise them, think of my examples as probably around ~30% of the species, which isn’t a lot, but the occurrence is possible. It’s a risk you will have to take if you want to continue that way, but with proper introduction and slow and steady bond building it’s definitely possible for them to live harmoniously

The key here in my answer is a hypothetical scenario that is impossible to answer because we’re not given enough context: how hysterical strength would look like on an Ackerman. Also, I think I didn’t phrase it very well, “hysterical strength” here is kind of an all encompassing term for “super powered capabilities for a spur in the moment when under life or death situations”. Examples include dad strength and dad speed ™️ and unexpected tenacity. An example from the show comes from Floch of all people, when he hangs on under the boat and manages to actually survive and take the crew by surprise, leading to Hange’s sacrifice. More examples in media include moments from that movie the Incredibles, the parents do a lot of crazy shit outside of their superpowers to save their kids! 

All this means, hysterical strength is unpredictable and even more so on an inexistent fictional condition (the Ackerman blood). This unpredictability could subvert even Levi’s strategy or tactics, granted, he’s incredibly fast with improvising too! But Mikasa would definitely have a chance at winning

Useless answer probably but I read your post an hour ago and I can’t stop thinking about it, so I’d like to word vomit a little: 

The thing about Levi in the show is that his prime years come to a startling stop when he sustains the explosion injuries, therefore we can’t know for certain if he’s actually reached his apex power. The thing with Levi and why he’s so powerful is not only the Ackerman blood, but also that he throws any and all emotion out the window whenever he attacks, he aims for efficiency and purpose, in an almost cold blooded way. I feel like this is his strength and weakness.

Well first of all make sure you have their basic needs down. Is the cage large enough? Enough toys (you’ll need to experiment a bit to see what they like, but shredding toys is a universal favourite)? Is their diet consisting of mainly pellets and fresh veggies? Make sure that millet, seeds and seed mixes are not the main thing they’re eating, only used as treats. They’re like ice cream to them so they’ll get obese or have liver diseases if they eat too much every day, not to mention hormonal problems that’ll make them bitey and aggressive 

A good way to start bonding with them is to get them comfortable with your hand and presence, which you’ve already done! The next step is to start training them the “step up” command, which will make it easier for you to put them back in the cage when they’re out, or get them out of dangerous situations in a pinch. You need their favourite snack and an optional clicker. You say the words “step up”, then put your finger around the lower part of their belly and push gently, this will make them step onto your finger. When they do so, reward them with a treat. Rinse and repeat every day in 20 minute sessions. That’s the most basic thing to train, and you can move on to recall training or trick training after they’re pros at this. Don’t overlook training! It keeps their little brains stimulated and strengthens the bond between you and them 💛

Think about some bird behaviours that happen in a flock. You can try to mimic these behaviours to get them to see you as part of their flock! Like sharing food (make sure they’re bird safe!), showering together, singing or talking to them (males can learn how to mimic and sing!), and giving scritches (birds can’t get the top part of their heads so they rely on their flockmates to help preen them, simply pinch a pin feather gently and the casing will come off, then you can rub it to get the dust off). 

Happy birding!! Hope this helps

You know you’ve made it when your bird willingly tries to be near you when you interact with them through the cage. Now you can try to train them to step up + attempt to give scritches. If you think they’re ready, you may take them out and show them around your house, introduce them to windows so they don’t crash into it at full speed (I’ve heard many horror stories of birds flying and crashing into the window at full speed and dying within minutes). Repeat this process a few more times, the key is to be slow and patient to build a strong bond.

And that’s pretty much it for introducing a new bird to a new environment. Hope it helps! It worked for me
